The problem describes an absorption line with energy 3.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV observed towards structures at ~2.1 Gpc. The rest energy of the 21 cm hyperfine transition of neutral hydrogen (HI) is 5.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV. At a redshift z ≈ 0.5 (corresponding to 2.1 Gpc for typical cosmological parameters), the observed energy is 5.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV / (1 + 0.5) ≈ 3.9 × 10⁻⁶ eV. The line is thus the redshifted 21 cm HI line.

In the Milky Way, the 21 cm line can be seen both in emission and absorption. Absorption features against bright background radio sources are predominantly produced by the cold neutral atomic medium (CNM), which has a low spin temperature and sufficient optical depth to create narrow absorption lines. The warm atomic medium is mostly seen in emission, and molecular clouds do not emit or absorb the 21 cm line. Therefore, the observed 21 cm absorption line is most likely associated with the cold atomic interstellar medium.

Answer: C
